topic: What if light kept getting slower every hour?

script.text: Here's how it works. Light is the fastest thing in the universe. Three hundred thousand kilometers every second. Seven and a half times around the Earth in one blink. That's real.
Then, on a Monday morning at seven o'clock, it halves. And every hour after that, on the hour, it halves again.

The rules. Only light slows down, and everything that travels like light. Radio. Wi-Fi. Phone signals. GPS. Your body, electricity and everything made of atoms still work fine. Otherwise this would be a very short video.

And one more rule, the oldest one in physics. Everything you see has already happened. Light only ever shows you the past. Today, it's a billionth of a second ago. You'd never notice. Remember that rule. Because it's about to get very, very noticeable.

science.claim: Light travels about 300,000 km every second, about 7.5 times around the Earth.
science.working: The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 m/s by definition; Earth's equatorial circumference is 40,075 km, so 299,792/40,075 = 7.48 laps per second.
science.source: NIST, 'Speed of light in vacuum' (CODATA); NASA Earth Fact Sheet
